purpose: OWNER 5557988072 item 6 -- declared venue maintenance intervals. An outage whose first error falls inside a declared window is classified scheduled_maintenance (planned venue outage), never an L5 fidelity failure, a collector defect or strategy behaviour. Windows are declared from an owner statement or the venue's own notice; the campaign never infers one from errors.
rules: declared windows are read-only inputs to diagnostics: no gate, cap, admission or policy change depends on them

the recovery sequence after a window is unchanged: account read healthy -> orphan-order reconcile before any mutation -> public prints resume vs the pre-outage baseline (or recorder tape) -> resume the bounded validation

timed-interval evidence is never formed across a window (intervals are only between consecutive unique decisions of one session); decisions time-stamped inside a window are reported as a provenance anomaly, never counted as cadence evidence
windows are appended, never edited after their end

windows.note: start is the first observed 503; the owner declared maintenance until 06:00 ET. Prints after end_utc still have to pass the recovery gate before any session.

revisions.note: the venue extended its own maintenance; the original end_utc is kept, the overrun is measured against the latest revised end, and the actual boundary stays the first healthy account read (venue_recovered 2026-09-06T10:52:18Z, prints gate still waiting)

open_at_window_start_UNKNOWN.state: last observed still_open AND unreadable; whether they rested, filled, cancelled or were rejected across the window is UNKNOWN and must be established by the recovery sequence before any mutation
open_at_window_start_UNKNOWN.resolution: RESOLVED at the ORDER LAYER. All fourteen carry a venue-authored terminal state in their own end_reason: rejected:ORDER_REJECTED_ZERO_FILL:<id>:ORDER_STATE_REJECTED:fields=action=ORDER_ACTION_BUY;avgPx=0.0000;cashOrderQty=0.00. ORDER_STATE_REJECTED is terminal -- a rejected order never rests, so it cannot fill later -- and the venue states avgPx 0.0000 and cashOrderQty 0.00 per order. Supporting, not load-bearing: the 11:36:22Z authenticated sweep returned seen 0 / cancelled [] / foreign [] / errors [], and the durable ledger records zero fills on all four markets. The reconciler marked them unreadable+still_open with open_orders_block_flat_claim true because its confirming GET hit the 503 -- it was more cautious than its own evidence warranted, which is the correct direction to fail. NOT ESTABLISHED: no per-market authenticated POSITION read and no trade-activity walk was performed for these four slugs; they were never re-selected after recovery. Verdict RECOVERY_FLAT_ORDER_CONFIRMED, not bare RECOVERY_FLAT.
open_at_window_start_UNKNOWN.orders_count_correction: Previously reported as TEN throughout this incident. The per-market figures (4/2/4/4) were right and their total was not: 4+2+4+4 = 14. Counted from the fill_reconciliation.reconciled.still_open id lists.
open_at_window_start_UNKNOWN.withdrawn_evidence: An earlier version of this record cited unchanged daily_realized_pnl_usd (-15.3350 before and after) as proof nothing filled in the blind window. THAT INFERENCE IS WITHDRAWN AND INVALID: that figure moves only on venue-confirmed SETTLEMENT, so a fill on an unsettled market would leave it untouched. The figure is accurate; it is not evidence about fills.

windows.recovery_requirement: unchanged from the rules above: account read healthy -> orphan-order reconcile BEFORE any mutation -> RECOVERY_FLAT only when authenticated venue state and durable ledger agree on zero open/orphan orders and zero unaccounted inventory. Any fill discovered inside the window is reconciled into the durable ledger first and routed through the existing held-position logic.
windows.observed_recovery_note: The venue recovered 1417.6 s (23 m 37.6 s) BEFORE the declared end. start_utc/end_utc are left exactly as declared and are NOT edited: the `revisions` mechanism takes max(declared, revised) by design, so it can only record a venue EXTENDING its window, never an early return. This field is descriptive only -- the loader ignores it -- and it exists so the declared window and the observed one are both on the record. NOT an overrun; SCHEDULED_MAINTENANCE_OVERRUN was never raised.
